title: Structure-Based Drug–Drug Interaction Prediction from Morgan Fingerprints: A Degree-Controlled and Cold-Start Evaluation of a Random Forest Baseline
content: Drug–drug interaction (DDI) checkers can only look up combinations that have already been recorded, so they say nothing about pairs that were never studied together, such as those involving newly approved drugs. We ask how much of the apparent performance of a structure-only DDI model survives a careful evaluation. Each drug is represented by Morgan (ECFP) fingerprints and ten physicochemical descriptors computed from PubChem SMILES (1,688 of 1,701 drugs in a DrugBank-derived list resolved), and a drug pair by order-invariant combinations of the two drugs’ features. We first show that a common negative sampling protocol, which screens random negatives only against the sampled positives, labels 20.9 ± 0.8% of its “non-interacting” pairs with recorded interactions. We then build two balanced benchmarks of 17,522 pairs whose negatives exclude every recorded pair: one with random negatives and one with degree-matched negatives. On the random-negative benchmark a control that uses only drug identity, with no chemistry, reaches ROC-AUC 0.758, comparable to Random Forests on fingerprints (0.753–0.768). On the degree-matched benchmark the control falls to or below chance, the original concatenated-fingerprint model drops to AUC 0.572, and the order-invariant feature set with descriptors reaches AUC 0.678 (accuracy 62.1%) on random pairs and 0.615 (accuracy 57.6%) when both drugs are unseen in training. Calibration, selective prediction and a ten-pair case panel show that the model misses many recorded interactions (for example Sildenafil + Nitroglycerin) and is best used with an explicit “uncertain” output, which a Streamlit prototype provides. This work is a research prototype and is not intended for clinical use.
